ai.description: This 30 mm frog is jet black with bright orange-red tubercles scattered across its dorsum. It is distinguished by a stout, globular body and lacks visible tympana.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Melanobatrachus indicus* is uniquely identified by its jet-black body adorned with distinct, bright orange or red tubercles, setting it apart from other Indian microhylids.
ai.habitat: *Melanobatrachus indicus* inhabits the high-altitude evergreen rainforests and shola grasslands of the southern Western Ghats, typically at elevations above 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: *Melanobatrachus indicus* is primarily nocturnal and exhibits a defensive strategy of curling into a ball to expose its bright orange-spotted, toxic-looking underside.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Melanobatrachus indicus* breeds during the monsoon season, laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs in hidden terrestrial nests or rock crevices.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Melanobatrachus indicus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats, specifically occurring in high-elevation forests (above 1,000m) across Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Melanobatrachus indicus* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps emitted from within dense leaf litter in montane forests.
